title: I2C LCD
summary: In Lesson 3, you learned that libraries supercharge code by bundling complex hardware protocols into friendly functions.

steps.title: I2C LCD

quickCheck.question: Which standard library header file must be included in your Arduino sketch to provide I2C communication functions?
quickCheck.explanation: <Wire.h> is the built-in Arduino library that manages the ATmega328P Two-Wire Interface (I2C) hardware.
quickCheck.warmupExplanation: Recall Lesson 3: libraries provide pre-written driver code, and <Wire.h> is the universal Arduino library for I2C.

quickCheck.question: In the declaration LiquidCrystal_I2C lcd(0x27, 16, 2);, what information does the first argument 0x27 provide?
options: The 7-bit I2C bus hardware address of the display backpack.
The refresh rate of the LCD in frames per second.
The pin number where the contrast knob is connected.
quickCheck.explanation: The first parameter defines the I2C hardware address (0x27) so the library communicates with the correct physical backpack on the bus.
quickCheck.warmupExplanation: In Step 4, we saw that every I2C device requires its specific 7-bit address to respond to incoming bus packets.
